$comment: Written from general knowledge for India. Not reviewed by a lawyer. Helpline buttons always come from here, never from the model.

guides.title: Morphed or leaked photos
steps: Do not delete anything. Take screenshots that show the post, the account name, the link and the date.
Report the post on the platform as non-consensual intimate imagery. Most platforms remove it faster under that label.
If the images are real and intimate, create a case on StopNCII.org so partner platforms block them from being posted.
File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930. You can report anonymously for this kind of content.
Publishing such images is an offence under IT Act sections 66E and 67A. Any police station must register your FIR.
Tell someone you trust. You did nothing wrong; the person who shared them did.

guides.title: Blackmail or sextortion
steps: Do not pay and do not send anything more. Paying almost always leads to more demands.
Stop replying, but do not delete the chat. Screenshot every message, the profile, the phone number and any payment details they gave.
Report the account on the platform, then block it. Make your profiles private and review who can see your friends list.
If they have real intimate images, create a case on StopNCII.org so partner platforms block them from being posted.
Call 1930 or file at cybercrime.gov.in. This is extortion (BNS section 308) and, if images are involved, IT Act sections 66E and 67A. Any police station must register your FIR.
Tell someone you trust. The threat works by keeping you alone and ashamed; it loses most of its power once someone else knows.

guides.title: Online stalking or harassment
steps: Keep everything: screenshots with dates, usernames, profile links and phone numbers.
Block and report each account. New accounts from the same person are worth noting too.
Lock down your profiles: private accounts, hide your phone number, turn off location in posts.
Check your phone for unknown apps and change passwords, with two-step login on email and social media.
Repeatedly following or contacting a woman online after she said no is stalking under BNS section 78. Report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930.

guides.title: Being followed
steps: If you feel in danger right now, call 112.
Go towards people and light: a shop, a petrol pump, a pharmacy, a hotel lobby. Do not go home if they are behind you.
Cross the road or change direction once. If they do the same, you are being followed.
Start Active duty in Winger so your location is shared and the walk is recorded.
Tell a shopkeeper or a guard. Ask them to wait with you while you call someone.
Note what they look like, their clothes and any vehicle number.

guides.title: Street harassment
steps: Your safety first. Move away and towards other people if you can.
Say it loudly and clearly if you feel safe to: "Stop touching me." It draws attention to him, not you.
On a bus or metro, tell the conductor, guard or the women's coach. Metro stations have help points.
If you can, note the time, place, bus or coach number and what he looked like.
Unwanted touching or sexual remarks are sexual harassment under BNS section 75. You can file a complaint at any police station.

guides.title: After a sexual assault
steps: Get to a safe place and call someone you trust, or 112.
Go to a hospital as soon as you can. Treatment and the medical exam must be free at any hospital, government or private.
If you can, do not wash, change or throw away clothes before the exam. It helps the case, but your care comes first.
You can file an FIR at any police station (Zero FIR). A woman officer should record your statement.
One Stop Centres (call 181) give medical, legal and counselling help in one place.
What happened is not your fault.

guides.title: Violence at home
steps: If you are in danger now, call 112. Turn on Home mode in Winger so alerts stay silent.
Keep copies of your ID, phone numbers and some money somewhere outside the home or with someone you trust.
Photograph injuries and see a doctor; the medical record helps later.
Call 181. They can connect you to a Protection Officer and a shelter.
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 lets a magistrate order protection, residence and money for you, without a criminal case.
Plan an exit route and a code word with one trusted person.

guides.title: Harassment at work
steps: Write down each incident: date, time, place, what was said or done, and who saw it.
Keep messages and emails. Forward copies to a personal account.
Complain in writing to your company's Internal Committee (POSH Act 2013), ideally within three months of the incident.
If there is no committee, or it is your employer, complain to the Local Committee at your district office.
You are protected from retaliation for complaining.

guides.title: Police refusing an FIR
steps: Ask politely but firmly for the FIR to be registered. For a serious offence, police must register it.
You can file at any police station. They must register a Zero FIR and transfer it.
Give the complaint in writing and ask for a stamped copy as proof you came.
If they still refuse, send the complaint to the Superintendent of Police by post or email.
You can also approach a magistrate, or file an e-FIR on your state police website for some offences.

guides.title: Unsafe cab or auto
steps: Start Set route or Active duty in Winger so your location is watched.
Share the trip from the ride app and use its SOS button.
Call someone and talk on speaker, naming the car number and where you are.
If the driver goes off route, ask him to stop at a busy place and get out there.
If you feel in danger, call 112.

guides.title: Acid attack
steps: Call 112. Rinse the area with lots of clean running water for at least 20 minutes.
Remove clothes and jewellery from the area unless stuck to the skin.
Go to the nearest hospital. Every hospital, government or private, must give free first aid and treatment.
The police must register an FIR. You are entitled to compensation.

guides.title: Someone claiming to be police
steps: Police do not arrest anyone over a video call. "Digital arrest" is a scam. Hang up.
Never pay money or share OTPs, bank details or Aadhaar with a caller.
In person, ask for name, rank and ID, and call 112 to check.
A woman should not be arrested after sunset or before sunrise except in exceptional cases with a woman officer and a magistrate's permission.
Report the call at cybercrime.gov.in or 1930.
